038    /**
039     * Check equality in a null-friendly fashion.
040     *
041     * @param a an object
042     * @param b an object to compare with a
043     * @return true if and only if a equals b, false otherwise
044     */
045    public static boolean equals(Object a, Object b) {
046        return (a == b) || (a != null && a.equals(b));

052     * @param o the object to compute the hash for

056        return o != null ? o.hashCode() : 0;

059    public static int permutation(int n, int r) {
060        if (n < 0) {
061            throw new IllegalArgumentException();
062        }
063        int permutation = 1;
064        for (int i = 0; i < r; i++) {
065            permutation *= n - i;
066        }
067        return permutation;
068    }

070    public static <X> Stream<Pair<X, X>> pairwise(Stream<X> a, Stream<X> b) {
071        // A stream can only be consumed once, but b is paired with every element of a.
072        List<X> bs = b.collect(Collectors.toList());
073        return a.flatMap(i -> bs.stream().map(j -> new Pair<>(i, j)));
074    }

076    /**
077     * @param low the lowest integer in the range
078     * @param high the highest integer in the range
079     * @return an array of all the values between low (inclusive) and high
080     * (inclusive) in order
081     */
082    public static int[] range(int low, int high) {
083        if (low > high) {
084            throw new IllegalArgumentException();
085        }
086        int[] range = new int[high - low + 1];
087        for (int i = 0; i < range.length; i++) {
088            range[i] = i + low;
089        }
090        return range;
091    }

093    /**
094     * @param from the lowest integer in the range
095     * @param to the integer after the highest integer in the range
096     * @return an array of all the values between from (inclusive) and to
097     * (exclusive) in order
098     */
099    public static int[] fromTo(int from, int to) {
100        if (from > to) {
101            throw new IllegalArgumentException();
102        }
103        int[] range = new int[to - from];
104        for (int i = 0; i < range.length; i++) {
105            range[i] = i + from;
106        }
107        return range;
108    }

132    private static int[] boolIndices(boolean[] bs, boolean val) {
133        int count = 0;
134        for (boolean b : bs) {
135            if (b == val) {
136                count++;
137            }
138        }
139        int[] vals = new int[count];
140        count = 0;
141        for (int i = 0; i < bs.length && count < vals.length; i++) {
142            if (bs[i] == val) {
143                vals[count++] = i;
144            }
145        }
146        assert count == vals.length;
147        return vals;
148    }

150    /**
151     * Randomly shuffle an array in place.
152     *
153     * @param <T> the type of the elements
154     * @param array the array to shuffle
155     * @param rand the random number generator
156     */
157    public static <T> void shuffle(T[] array, Random rand) {
158        for (int i = 0; i < array.length; i++) {
159            int index = rand.nextInt(array.length);
160            // Simple swap
161            T temp = array[index];
162            array[index] = array[i];
163            array[i] = temp;
164        }
165    }

167    /**
168     * Reverse part of an array in place.
169     *
170     * @param array the array to reverse
171     * @param to reverse from index 0 to here
172     */
173    public static void reverse(int[] array, int to) {
174        for (int j = 0; j < to / 2; j++) {
175            int temp = array[j];
176            array[j] = array[to - j - 1];
177            array[to - j - 1] = temp;
178        }
179    }
180

186    public static void reverse(int[] array) {

250    public static <T> Optional<T> findUnique(T[] array, Predicate<T> predicate) {
251        Optional<T> i = Optional.empty();
252        for (T t : array) {
253            if (predicate.test(t)) {
254                if (i.isPresent()) {
255                    return Optional.empty();
256                }
257                i = Optional.of(t);
258            }
259        }
260        return i;
261    }
262
263    public static OptionalInt findUnique(PrimitiveIterator.OfInt iter, IntPredicate predicate) {
264        OptionalInt i = OptionalInt.empty();
265        while (iter.hasNext()) {
266            int val = iter.nextInt();
267            if (predicate.test(val)) {
268                if (i.isPresent()) {
269                    return OptionalInt.empty();
270                }
271                i = OptionalInt.of(val);
272            }
273        }
274        return i;
275    }

286    /**
287     * @param item count the number of elements in the array no greater than
288     * this item
289     * @param array the array assumed to be sorted
290     * @return the number of elements in the array no greater than the item
291     */
292    public static int ordinal(int item, int[] array) {
293        int from = 0;
294        int to = array.length;
295
296        while (from < to) {
297            int mid = (from + to) >>> 1;
298            int midVal = array[mid];
299
300            if (midVal < item) {
301                from = mid + 1;
302            } else if (midVal > item) {
303                to = mid;
304            } else {
305                assert item >= array[mid];
306                return mid + 1;
307            }
308        }
309        return from;
310    }

312    /**
313     * Check if every element in the array is unique.
314     *
315     * @param array the array
316     * @return {@code true} if and only if the elements in the array never
317     * repeat, {@code false} otherwise
318     */
319    public static boolean isUnique(int[] array) {
320        for (int i = 0; i < array.length; i++) {
321            for (int j = i + 1; j < array.length; j++) {
322                if (array[i] == array[j]) {
323                    return false;
324                }
325            }
326        }
327        return true;
328    }

336     * repeat, {@code false} otherwise

338    public static <T> boolean isUnique(T[] array) {

341                if (equals(array[i], array[j])) {
342                    return false;
343                }
344            }
345        }
346        return true;

349    /**
350     * Functional-programming cons. Nondestructive.
351     *
352     * @param <T> the type of the elements
353     * @param head the beginning of the new list
354     * @param tail the end of the new list
355     * @return a copy of the original list with head appended at the start
356     */
357    public static <T> List<T> cons(T head, List<? extends T> tail) {
358        List<T> r = new ArrayList<>(tail.size() + 1);
359        r.add(head);
360        r.addAll(tail);
361        return r;
362    }
363
364    /**
365     * Functional-programming snoc. Nondestructive.
366     *
367     * @param <T> the type of the elements
368     * @param head the beginning of the new list
369     * @param tail the end of the new list
370     * @return a copy of the original list with tail appended at the end
371     */
372    public static <T> List<T> snoc(List<? extends T> head, T tail) {
373        List<T> r = new ArrayList<>(head.size() + 1);
374        r.addAll(head);
375        r.add(tail);
376        return r;
377    }

379    /**
380     * Append the item at the start of the array. Nondestructive.
381     *
382     * @param <T> the type of the elements
383     * @param item the beginning of the new array
384     * @param array the end of the new array
385     * @return a copy of the original array with item appended at the start
386     */
387    public static <T> T[] cons(T item, T[] array) {
388        T[] r = Arrays.copyOf(array, array.length + 1);
389        for (int i = r.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
390            r[i] = r[i - 1];
391        }
392        r[0] = item;
393        return r;
394    }
395
396    /**
397     * Append the item at the end of the array. Nondestructive.

402     * @return a copy of the original array with item appended at the end
403     */
404    public static <T> T[] snoc(T[] array, T item) {
405        T[] r = Arrays.copyOf(array, array.length + 1);
406        r[array.length] = item;
407        return r;
408    }

437    /**
438     * Functional-programming cons if head is present. Nondestructive.
439     *
440     * @param <T> the type of the elements
441     * @param head the beginning of the new list if present
442     * @param tail the end of the new list
443     * @return a copy of the original list with head appended at the start if
444     * present, otherwise a copy of tail
445     */
446    public static <T> List<T> maybeCons(Optional<T> head, List<? extends T> tail) {
447        return head.map(h -> cons(h, tail)).orElse(new ArrayList<>(tail));
448    }

450    /**
451     * Concatenates all the arrays in the given order into one array. Must be
452     * supplied at least one array. Nondestructive.
453     *
454     * @param <T> the type of the elements
455     * @param arrays the array of arrays
456     * @return the concatenation of all the arrays
457     */
458    public static <T> T[] concat(T[][] arrays) {
459        switch (arrays.length) {
460            case 0:
461                @SuppressWarnings("unchecked") T[] empty = (T[]) Array.newInstance(arrays.getClass().getComponentType().getComponentType(), 0);
462                return empty;
463            case 1:
464                return arrays[0];
465            default:
466                int length = 0;
467                for (T[] array : arrays) {
468                    length += array.length;
469                }
470                int offset = 0;
471                @SuppressWarnings("unchecked") T[] concat = (T[]) Array.newInstance(arrays.getClass().getComponentType().getComponentType(), length);
472                for (T[] array : arrays) {
473                    System.arraycopy(array, 0, concat, offset, array.length);
474                    offset += array.length;
475                }
476                return concat;
477        }
478    }

480    /**
481     * Repeat the item.
482     *
483     * @param <T> the type of the item
484     * @param item the item
485     * @param times the number of times to repeat
486     * @return an array containing only the item
487     */
488    public static <T> T[] replicate(T item, int times) {
489        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
490        T[] array = (T[]) Array.newInstance(item.getClass(), times);
491        for (int i = 0; i < array.length; i++) {
492            array[i] = item;
493        }
494        return array;
495    }

497    /**
498     * Returns all permutations of picking a fixed number of distinct elements
499     * in the array.
500     *
501     * @param <T> the type of the elements
502     * @param array the array
503     * @param choose the number of elements to pick
504     * @return the permutations
505     */
506    public static <T> T[][] permutations(T[] array, int choose) {
507        if (choose > array.length) {
508            throw new IllegalArgumentException();
509        }
510        if (choose == 0) {
511            @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
512            T[][] permutations = (T[][]) Array.newInstance(array.getClass(), 1);
513            @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
514            T[] permutation = (T[]) Array.newInstance(array.getClass().getComponentType(), 0);
515            permutations[0] = permutation;
516            return permutations;
517        }
518
519        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
520        T[][] permutations = (T[][]) Array.newInstance(
521                array.getClass().getComponentType(),
522                permutation(array.length, choose), choose);
523
524        int[] indices = new int[choose];
525        indices[indices.length - 1]--;
526        for (T[] permutation : permutations) {
527            do {
528                int j = indices.length - 1;
529                indices[j]++;
530                while (indices[j] >= array.length) {
531                    indices[j] = 0;
532                    j--;
533                    indices[j]++;
534                }
535            } while (!isUnique(indices));
536            for (int k = 0; k < indices.length; k++) {
537                permutation[k] = array[indices[k]];
538            }
539        }
540        return permutations;
541    }
542
543    /**
544     * Returns all possibilities of picking a fixed number of elements in the
545     * array.
546     *
547     * @param <T> the type of the elements
548     * @param array the array
549     * @param choose the number of elements to pick
550     * @return the sequence
551     */
552    public static <T> T[][] sequence(T[] array, int choose) {
553        if (choose <= 0) {
554            throw new IllegalArgumentException();
555        }
556        return sequence(replicate(array, choose));
557    }
558
559    /**
560     * Returns all possibilities of picking one element in each array. Similar
561     * to Haskell's {@code sequence} for lists, except for edge cases.
562     *
563     * @param <T> the type of the elements
564     * @param arrays the arrays
565     * @return the sequence
566     */
567    public static <T> T[][] sequence(T[][] arrays) {
568        if (arrays.length == 0) {
569            @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
570            T[][] sequence = (T[][]) Array.newInstance(arrays.getClass().getComponentType(), 1);
571            @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
572            T[] permutation = (T[]) Array.newInstance(arrays.getClass().getComponentType().getComponentType(), 0);
573            sequence[0] = permutation;
574            return sequence;
575        }
576
577        int product = 1;
578        for (T[] array : arrays) {
579            product *= array.length;
580        }
581        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
582        T[][] sequence = (T[][]) Array.newInstance(
583                arrays.getClass().getComponentType().getComponentType(),
584                product, arrays.length);
585
586        int[] indices = new int[arrays.length];
587        indices[indices.length - 1]--;
588        for (T[] array : sequence) {
589            int j = indices.length - 1;
590            indices[j]++;
591            while (indices[j] >= arrays[j].length) {
592                indices[j] = 0;
593                j--;
594                indices[j]++;
595            }
596            for (int k = 0; k < indices.length; k++) {
597                array[k] = arrays[k][indices[k]];
598            }
599        }
600        return sequence;
601    }

603    /**
604     * Returns a sublist from index 0 to the index of the item (inclusive).
605     * Equivalent to the Haskell code {@code takeWhile (== item) list}
606     *
607     * @param <T> the element type
608     * @param item the item to find
609     * @param list the list of items
610     * @return a prefix of the {@code list} ending at the first {@code item} if
611     * found, otherwise the entire list
612     */
613    public static <T> List<T> takeUntil(T item, List<T> list) {
614        int index = 0;
615        for (T t : list) {
616            index++;
617            if (item.equals(t)) {
618                return list.subList(0, index);
619            }
620        }
621        return list;
622    }
623
624    /**
625     * Returns a sublist from the index of the item (inclusive) to the end of
626     * the list. Equivalent to the Haskell code {@code dropWhile (/= item) list}
627     *
628     * @param <T> the element type
629     * @param item the item to find
630     * @param list the list of items
631     * @return a suffix of the {@code list} starting at the first {@code item}
632     * if found, otherwise the entire list
633     */
634    public static <T> List<T> dropUntil(T item, List<T> list) {
635        int index = 0;
636        for (T t : list) {
637            if (item.equals(t)) {
638                return list.subList(index, list.size());
639            }
640            index++;
641        }
642        return Collections.emptyList();
643    }

645    /**
646     * Checks if the list starts with specific elements.
647     *
648     * @param <T> the element type
649     * @param string the list
650     * @param prefix the starting elements of the list
651     * @return {@code true} if and only if {@code string} starts with
652     * {@code prefix}, {@code false} otherwise
653     */
654    public static <T> boolean startsWith(List<T> string, List<T> prefix) {
655        final int stringSize = string.size();
656        final int prefixSize = prefix.size();
657        if (prefixSize > stringSize) {
658            return false;
659        }
660        return prefix.equals(string.subList(0, prefixSize));
661    }
662
663    /**
664     * Checks if the list ends with specific elements.
665     *
666     * @param <T> the element type
667     * @param string the list
668     * @param suffix the ending elements of the list
669     * @return {@code true} if and only if {@code string} ends with
670     * {@code suffix}, {@code false} otherwise
671     */
672    public static <T> boolean endsWith(List<T> string, List<T> suffix) {
673        final int stringSize = string.size();
674        final int suffixSize = suffix.size();
675        if (suffixSize > stringSize) {
676            return false;
677        }
678        return suffix.equals(string.subList(stringSize - suffixSize, stringSize));
679    }

705    /**
706     * @param array an array of integers
707     * @return the minimum integer in the array
708     */
709    public static int min(int... array) {
710        if (array.length == 0) {
711            throw new IllegalArgumentException();
712        }
713        int min = array[0];
714        for (int i = 1; i < array.length; i++) {
715            min = Math.min(min, array[i]);
716        }
717        return min;
718    }

725        if (!iter.hasNext()) {
726            throw new IllegalArgumentException();
727        }
728        int min = iter.next();
729        while (iter.hasNext()) {
730            min = Math.min(min, iter.next());
731        }
732        return min;
733    }

750    /**
751     * @param iter an iterator of integers
752     * @return the maximum integer in the iterator
753     */
754    public static int max(TIntIterator iter) {
755        if (!iter.hasNext()) {
756            throw new IllegalArgumentException();
757        }
758        int max = iter.next();
759        while (iter.hasNext()) {
760            max = Math.max(max, iter.next());
761        }
762        return max;
763    }

765    /**
766     * @param a
767     * @param b
768     * @return the greatest common divisor of {@code a} and {@code b}
769     */
770    public static int gcd(int a, int b) {
771        return b == 0 ? a : gcd(b, a % b);
772    }
773
774    /**
775     * @param a
776     * @param b
777     * @return the greatest common divisor of {@code a} and {@code b}
778     */
779    public static long gcd(long a, long b) {
780        return b == 0 ? a : gcd(b, a % b);
781    }

783    /**
784     * @param a
785     * @param b
786     * @return the least common multiple of {@code a} and {@code b}
787     */
788    public static int lcm(int a, int b) {
789        return a * (b / gcd(a, b));
790    }

792    /**
793     * @param a
794     * @param b
795     * @return the least common multiple of {@code a} and {@code b}
796     */
797    public static long lcm(long a, long b) {
798        return a * (b / gcd(a, b));
799    }

801    public static int divFloor(int a, int b) {
802        if (b < 0) {
803            return divFloor(-a, -b);
804        } else if (a < 0) {
805            return (a - b + 1) / b;
806        }
807        return (a / b);
808    }
809
810    public static long divFloor(long a, long b) {
811        if (b < 0) {
812            return divFloor(-a, -b);
813        } else if (a < 0) {
814            return (a - b + 1) / b;
815        }
816        return (a / b);
817    }
818
819    public static int divCeil(int a, int b) {
820        if (b < 0) {
821            return divCeil(-a, -b);
822        } else if (a >= 0) {
823            return ((a + b - 1) / b);
824        }
825        return a / b;
826    }
827
828    public static long divCeil(long a, long b) {
829        if (b < 0) {
830            return divCeil(-a, -b);
831        } else if (a >= 0) {
832            return ((a + b - 1) / b);
833        }
834        return a / b;
835    }
836
837    /**
838     * Division rounded half away from zero, e.g. {@code 25 / 10 = 3} and
839     * {@code -25 / 10 = -3}.
840     *
841     * @param a the dividend
842     * @param b the divisor, not zero
843     * @return the rounded quotient
844     */
845    public static long divRound(long a, long b) {
846        long quotient = a / b;
847        long remainder = a % b;
848        if (2 * Math.abs(remainder) >= Math.abs(b)) {
849            quotient += (a < 0) == (b < 0) ? 1 : -1;
850        }
851        return quotient;
852    }

854    /**
855     * Enumerate the iterator and return the values discovered. The iterator is
856     * exhausted on return.
857     *
858     * @param iter an iterator
859     * @return the values found in the iterator
860     */
861    public static int[] iterate(IntIterator iter) {
862        TIntArrayList i = new TIntArrayList();
863        while (iter.hasNext()) {
864            i.add(iter.next());
865        }
866        return i.toArray();
867    }

869    /**
870     * @param <K> input type
871     * @param <V> return type
872     * @param map a bijection
873     * @return the inverse of map
874     */
875    public static <K, V> Map<V, K> inverse(Map<K, V> map) {
876        Map<V, K> inverse = new HashMap<>(map.size());
877        for (Entry<K, V> entry : map.entrySet()) {
878            if (inverse.put(entry.getValue(), entry.getKey()) != null) {
879                throw new IllegalArgumentException(map + " is not a bijection.");
880            }
881        }
882        return inverse;
883    }

885    /**
886     * Concatenate the string representation of the items with a comma
887     * separating each item.
888     *
889     * @param <T> the type of the elements
890     * @param items the items to display
891     * @return the items string form separated by commas
892     */
893    public static <T> String commaSeparate(T[] items) {
894        return intercalate(", ", items);
895    }

897    /**
898     * Concatenate the string representation of the items with a comma
899     * separating each item.
900     *
901     * @param items the items to display
902     * @return the items string form separated by commas
903     */
904    public static String commaSeparate(Iterable<?> items) {
905        return intercalate(", ", items);
906    }
907
908    /**
909     * Concatenate the string representation of the items with a separator
910     * separating each item.
911     *
912     * @param <T> the type of the elements
913     * @param separator the string to separate each item
914     * @param items the items to display
915     * @return the items string form separated by the separator
916     */
917    public static <T> String intercalate(String separator, T[] items) {
918        StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();
919        if (items.length > 0) {
920            result.append(items[0]);
921            for (int i = 1; i < items.length; i++) {
922                result.append(separator).append(items[i]);
923            }
924        }
925        return result.toString();
926    }
927
928    /**
929     * Concatenate the string representation of the items with a separator
930     * separating each item.
931     *
932     * @param separator the string to separate each item
933     * @param items the items to display
934     * @return the items string form separated by the separator
935     */
936    public static String intercalate(String separator, Iterable<?> items) {
937        StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();
938        Iterator<?> iter = items.iterator();
939        if (iter.hasNext()) {
940            result.append(iter.next());
941            while (iter.hasNext()) {
942                result.append(separator).append(iter.next());
943            }
944        }
945        return result.toString();
946    }

948    @SafeVarargs
949    public static <T> T[] cast(Object[] array, T... dest) {
950        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
951        T[] to = dest.length == array.length
952                ? dest
953                : (T[]) Array.newInstance(dest.getClass().getComponentType(), array.length);
954        System.arraycopy(array, 0, to, 0, to.length);
955        return to;
956    }

958    public static <T> Set<T> union(Set<T> a, Set<T> b) {
959        Set<T> union = new HashSet<>();
960        union.addAll(a);
961        union.addAll(b);
962        return union;
963    }
